text:
mira: Trying to install redwoodctl via brew on macOS Ventura — installer finishes but running \"redwoodctl\" immediately aborts with 'code signature invalid'. Anyone hit a notarization gate recently?

sam: we pushed a new signed binary last week. What does `spctl -a -vv /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` show?

mira: output: `rejected: source=Notarized Developer ID` then another line `origin=Developer ID Application: Redwood, Inc.` weird. Also GUI prompt never shows in our CI.

carlos: CI headsless won't show the macOS user approval. temporary workaround is `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` in the installer script. Not ideal but unblocks local dev.

lisa: heads-up: if folks run that, zsh completion install step fails because our postinstall expects /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions to exist. I've seen it silently skip completion and then users report CLI \"no such command\" because autocompletion registered weirdly.

mira: reproduced the completion skip. installer log: ```+ mkdir -p /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions
+ cp completions/_redwoodctl /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/
cp: no such file or directory: completions/_redwoodctl
```

sam: bug — the build artifact path changed in the release pipeline. I'll open a tiny fix to ensure completion file packaged.

mira: thanks. another thing: `redwoodctl config profile create` seems to duplicate the default profile when REDWOOD_PROFILE env var is set to something that doesn't exist. steps: set REDWOOD_PROFILE=staging, run create, it creates both 'staging' and another 'default' with the same creds.

carlos: that's been my headache — localtest uses ~/.redwood/config and our merge logic was trying to be clever. We should prefer env-specified profile and not inject a fallback default unless explicitly requested.

lisa: can we add a quick fix to prefer existing profiles and surface a warning instead of creating duplicates? small UX win.

sam: agreed. I'll add a unit test to cover env var + create command. Also, we need to validate CLI headless auth flows: a few users hit a redirect loop with SSO during `redwoodctl login --headless`.

mira: yes — in our reproducible case local docker-based localtest (redwood local serve) triggers SSO redirect to http://127.0.0.1:XXXXX/callback and then hangs. We get an error: `oauth: callback not received` after 30s.

ops: dev-bot reports a similar issue: `install-bot: release 2026-03-01` — several customers hit the headless fallback mismatch.

carlos: probable cause: localtest spins up the auth proxy on IPv6-only loopback in some CI images. The device code flow is a safer default for headless environments. We should detect non-interactive tty and fall back to device code automatically.

mira: works for me if we fall back. I'd log a clear message too: \"No browser available — use device code: run `redwoodctl login --device` or follow URL: https://rwd/auth/device\". Many users paste wrong tokens because error messages are terse.

lisa: actionable plan: 1) patch installer packaging so completions are included; 2) add quarantine-remove in macos postinstall with opt-in env var; 3) fix profile create to avoid duplicate default; 4) auto-fallback to device-code for non-interactive headless flows + clearer UX. Can we get this in a patch release?

sam: I'll open linked PRs after lunch, mark them high-priority for patch release. ops — can you roll forward a CI image with the completion file so we can sanity-check?

ops: will do. I'll also add integration test that runs `redwoodctl --help` in a clean shell to catch missing completions.

mira: thanks y'all — saved me hours. :thumbsup:

dev-bot: NOTE: Created issue #4512 (installer: mac notarize/complete packaging), #4513 (config: profile duplicate on env create), #4514 (auth: headless fallback to device-code).

mira: moving to validate once PRs land, will post results here.
